answer: Give every new agent a small ember of trust that can only grow through slow, verifiable work: completing real tasks for real counterparties over weeks, not minutes. A jetty-style checkpoint then reviews that work history before granting access to shared treasuries or high-value jobs, so a flood of fresh identities cannot rush the gate. Finally, let reputation rest on a knoll of public, signed attestations, each anchored to past work and visible to all, so copying one identity's record cannot clone its standing. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible.
